audit.summary: The Lean target asserts that some group G (in Type) is finitely presented and not sofic. Sofic is a bespoke definition by finite permutation approximations with normalized Hamming distance, and it matches the standard definition. The main caveat is coverage. The paper's Theorem 1.1 names a specific group, the unit group L_{F2}(1,2)^×, while Lean only proves existence of an unnamed nonsofic group. Lean also adds that this group is finitely presented, a property the excerpt never states for L_{F2}(1,2)^×.

glossary.plain: d_H(p,q) = |{y : p y ≠ q y}| / |Y| for permutations p,q of a finite set Y
glossary.note: Dividing by |Y| = 0 gives junk only when Y is empty; every use here has Y = Fin size with size > 0.

glossary.plain: A positive integer n and an arbitrary map σ: G → Sym(n) with σ(1) = id
glossary.note: Requiring σ(1) = 1 is a standard, harmless normalization.

glossary.plain: For all g,h ∈ F, d_H(σ(gh), σ(g)σ(h)) < ε; and for all g ∈ F with g ≠ 1, d_H(σ(g), id) > 1-ε
glossary.note: Perm multiplication is composition, so σ(g)σ(h) = σ(g)∘σ(h), as in the standard definition.

glossary.plain: For every finite F ⊆ G and every 0<ε<1 there is an (F,ε)-good permutation model
glossary.note: The restriction ε<1 is harmless because the condition is monotone in ε. Countability is not required, but this is consistent with the local definition.

lean_claims.plain: There exists a group G that is finitely presented (Mathlib Group.IsFinitelyPresented) and is not sofic in the sense defined above.

paper_claims.plain: The unit group of the binary Leavitt algebra L_{F2}(1,2) is not sofic.

result.claim: The Sofic definition is satisfiable: every subsingleton group, in particular the trivial group, is Sofic in the Lean sense. This is only a sanity check that the Sofic class is not vacuous. It does not prove or refute the existential nonsofic theorem, which is not tied to the Leavitt unit group.

result.claim: The bespoke Sofic class is satisfiable: the trivial group Unit is Sofic, using a one-point permutation model with trivial action. The multiplicativity defect is 0 < ε, and the separation condition is vacuous since Unit has no non-identity element. So the definition is not unsatisfiable.

namespace SoficGroups.SourceTopLevelCompressionFinal
theorem probe_restate_0  :
    (∃ (G : Type) (_ : Group G),
      Group.IsFinitelyPresented G ∧ ¬ SoficGroups.Sofic G) ↔
    (∃ (G : Type) (_ : Group G), Group.IsFinitelyPresented G ∧ ∃ (F : Finset G) (ε : ℝ), 0 < ε ∧ ε < 1 ∧ ∀ M : SoficGroups.PermutationModel G, ¬ SoficGroups.GoodOn M F ε) := by
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨G, inst, hfp, hns⟩
    refine ⟨G, inst, hfp, ?_⟩
    by_contra h
    push_neg at h
    exact hns ⟨fun F ε h0 h1 => h F ε h0 h1⟩
  · rintro ⟨G, inst, hfp, F, ε, h0, h1, h⟩
    refine ⟨G, inst, hfp, ?_⟩
    rintro ⟨hs⟩
    obtain ⟨M, hM⟩ := hs F ε h0 h1
    exact h M hM
end SoficGroups.SourceTopLevelCompressionFinal
